agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

json-tui
========

![Video](demo.webp)

A JSON visualizer with an interactive terminal UI.

Features
--------
- **Interactive**: Use keyboard or mouse to scroll/expand objects.
- **Colors**
- **Responsive**: Adapt to the terminal dimensions. Very long text values are
  wrapped on several lines.
- **Cross-platform**: Windows, Linux, MacOS.
- **Small**: ~0.7MB all included. Zero dependencies.
- The output is displayed inline with the previous commands. Meaning you can
  still see the json after leaving json-tui.
- *(Vim users): Also support `j`/`k` for navigation.*
- **Table view**: Turn arrays of objects into tables. <details>
  
  <summary>Video</summary>
  
  ![ezgif com-gif-maker (7)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/149676534-e73b2bcc-1eef-4dde-901e-8381e9ca8f87.gif)

</details>

Usage
-----

```bash
json-tui [OPTIONS] [FILE]
```

### Options

- `-f`, `--fullscreen` - Display JSON in fullscreen mode on the alternate buffer
- `-k`, `-key`, `-keybinding` - Display the supported keys
- `q` or `escape` - Quit the application
- Arrow keys, `j`/`k` - Navigate
- `gg`, `G` - Jump to top/bottom
- `-`, `+` - Collapse/expand

### Examples

```bash
# View a JSON file
json-tui data.json

# Pipe JSON from another command
cat data.json | json-tui

# View with fullscreen mode
json-tui --fullscreen data.json
```

Installation
------------

Pre-built binaries and packages are available for:
- Linux (deb, rpm, binary)
- MacOS
- Windows
- Snap package
- Arch Linux (AUR)

Similar projects
----------------
- https://github.com/antonmedv/fx
- https://github.com/skanehira/tson
- https://github.com/cielong/pyfx
</output>

# \x00\x1bP$q q\x1b\\ = null + DCS $q q + ST (string terminator) - cursor shape query
# \x1b[?7l = disable line wrap
# \x1b[?1000h = enable mouse
# \x1b[?1003h = enable mouse any event
# \x1b[?1015h = urxvt mouse
# \x1b[?1006h = SGR mouse
# \x00\r = null + CR
# \x1b[2K = clear line
# \x1b[7m{ \x1b[27m = reverse video { reset
# (spaces for padding)
# \r\r\n = CR CR LF (end of line)
# \x1b[2K OOPS wait - this line has spaces after {
# Then "a": 1
# Then }
# \x1b[2A = cursor up 2 lines
# \x1b[8D = cursor back 8 columns
# \x1b[?25l = hide cursor
# \x00 null
# \x1b[2B = cursor down 2 lines
# \x1b[8C = cursor right 8 columns
# \r\x1b[1A\x1b[1A = CR + up up
# \x1b[6n = cursor position request
# Then it re-renders the content
# Then cleanup: restore mouse, show cursor, etc.

# The rendering approach is:
# 1. Move to beginning of display area
# 2. Clear lines and write content
# 3. After writing, move cursor to current selected position (or hide it)

# The key insight: it renders the JSON tree INLINE (not fullscreen)
# The display takes up exactly as many lines as needed to show the visible content

# Let me understand the exact structure:
# Line 1: {    (or just the value if scalar)  
# Line 2:   "a": 1
# Line 3: }

# When navigating, it re-renders by going back to the top of the display and redrawing

# Now let me study a more complex example to understand scrolling
python3 -c "
import subprocess, sys, time, os
import pty, select

# Create a PTY with specific size
import fcntl, termios, struct

def set_winsize(fd, rows, cols):
    winsize = struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

master, slave = pty.openpty()
set_winsize(slave, 20, 80)  # 20 lines, 80 cols

proc = subprocess.Popen(['./executable', '/tmp/manyitems.json'], 
    stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, 
    close_fds=True)
os.close(slave)

time.sleep(0.5)
data = b''
try:
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        if not r:
            break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
except:
    pass

try:
    os.write(master, b'q')
    time.sleep(0.3)
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        if not r:
            break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
except:
    pass

try:
    proc.wait(timeout=2)
except:
    proc.kill()
try:
    os.close(master)
except:
    pass

print(repr(data[:3000]))
" 2>&1

import subprocess, sys, time, os
import pty, select
import fcntl, termios, struct

def set_winsize(fd, rows, cols):
    winsize = struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

master, slave = pty.openpty()
set_winsize(slave, 24, 80)  # 24 lines x 80 cols terminal

proc = subprocess.Popen(['./executable', '/tmp/tiny.json'], 
    stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, 
    close_fds=True)
os.close(slave)

time.sleep(0.5)
data = b''
try:
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        if not r:
            break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
except:
    pass

try:
    os.write(master, b'q')
    time.sleep(0.3)
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
        if not r:
            break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
except:
    pass

    proc.wait(timeout=2)
except:
    proc.kill()
try:
    os.close(master)
except:
    pass

lines = clean.replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '').split('\n')

def decode_esc(raw):
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(raw):
        c = raw[i]
        if c == 0x1b:
            j = i+1
            if j < len(raw) and raw[j] == ord('P'):
                k = raw.find(b'\x1b\\', j)
                if k == -1: k = len(raw)-2
                result.append(f'<DCS:{raw[i+2:k].decode("latin1","replace")}>')

                while k < len(raw) and (raw[k] < 0x40 or raw[k] > 0x7e):

                seq = raw[j+1:k+1].decode('latin1','replace')
                result.append(f'<CSI:{seq}>')
                i = k+1
                continue
            elif j < len(raw) and raw[j] == ord('\\'):
                result.append('<ST>')
                i += 2
                continue
            result.append('<ESC>')
            i += 1
        elif c == 0: result.append('<NUL>'); i += 1
        elif c == 13: result.append('<CR>'); i += 1
        elif c == 10: result.append('<LF>'); i += 1

# Now I have a very clear picture of the behavior:
# Inline mode:
# - Draw min(content_lines, terminal_height) lines
# - Lines padded to min(max_content_width, terminal_width)
# - No alternate screen
# - Leave output visible after quit

# Fullscreen mode:
# - Use alternate screen (?1049h/?1049l)  
# - Draw exactly terminal_height lines
# - Lines padded to terminal_width
# - Clear after quit (alternate screen restores)

# Now let me understand the cursor/input handling
# After initial render, cursor is hidden and positioned
# Input is read in raw mode

# Let me also study the rendering protocol more carefully:
# After each render, cursor goes back to start of display area
# On quit: restore cursor, clear mouse, exit raw mode

# Let me look at how the first render works vs subsequent redraws
python3 << 'EOF'
import subprocess, time, os
import pty, select
import fcntl, termios, struct, re

def set_winsize(fd, rows, cols):
    winsize = struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

master, slave = pty.openpty()
set_winsize(slave, 10, 80)

proc = subprocess.Popen(['./executable', '/tmp/simple2.json'], 
    stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
os.close(slave)
time.sleep(0.3)
data = b''
try:
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.05)
        if not r: break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk: break
        data += chunk
except: pass

# Send down key
os.write(master, b'\x1b[B')  # down arrow
time.sleep(0.2)
try:
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.05)
        if not r: break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk: break
        data += chunk
except: pass

os.write(master, b'q')
time.sleep(0.2)
try:
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.05)
        if not r: break
        chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        if not chunk: break
        data += chunk
except: pass
try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
except: proc.kill()
os.close(master)

def decode_esc(raw):
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(raw):
        c = raw[i]
        if c == 0x1b:
            j = i+1
            if j < len(raw) and raw[j] == ord('P'):
                k = raw.find(b'\x1b\\', j)
                if k == -1: k = len(raw)-2
                result.append(f'<DCS:{raw[i+2:k].decode("latin1","replace")}>')
                i = k+2
            elif j < len(raw) and raw[j] == ord('['):
                k = j+1
                while k < len(raw) and (raw[k] < 0x40 or raw[k] > 0x7e):
                    k += 1
                seq = raw[j+1:k+1].decode('latin1','replace')
                result.append(f'<CSI:{seq}>')
                i = k+1
            elif j < len(raw) and raw[j] == ord('\\'):
                result.append('<ST>')
                i += 2
            else: result.append('<ESC>'); i += 1
        elif c == 0: result.append('<NUL>'); i += 1
        elif c == 13: result.append('<CR>'); i += 1
        elif c == 10: result.append('<LF>'); i += 1
        else: result.append(chr(c)); i += 1
    return ''.join(result)

print(decode_esc(data))

// Full draw: position + CPR + render + back to top + hide cursor
void full_draw(App& app, bool first_draw=false) {
    std::string pos_seq;
    if(!first_draw) {
        // Go to bottom of previous display
        if(app.prev_lines>1){pos_seq+="\x1b[";pos_seq+=std::to_string(app.prev_lines-1);pos_seq+="B";}
        if(app.prev_width>0){pos_seq+="\x1b[";pos_seq+=std::to_string(app.prev_width);pos_seq+="C";}
        pos_seq+="\r";
        for(int i=0;i<app.prev_lines-1;i++) pos_seq+="\x1b[1A";
        pos_seq+="\x1b[6n";
        // First draw: null + CR + clear first line
        pos_seq+='\x00'; pos_seq+="\r\x1b[2K";
    }
    write_all(pos_seq);

    auto [nl,fw]=do_render(app);
    app.prev_lines=nl; app.prev_width=fw;

    // Back to top
    std::string back;
</output>

    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

    try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk

# So maybe the CPR is just for RESIZE detection, not normal operation

extra = b''

    r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
    if not r: break
    try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); extra += chunk
    except: break

print(f"After CPR response: {len(extra)} bytes")

    print(repr(extra[:100]))

print(f"Data2 first 100: {repr(data2[:100])}")

import subprocess, time, os

#

# 
# Actually: I think FTXUI uses CPR (cursor position) to know the ABSOLUTE position
# After receiving CPR, it knows where the display starts
# Then it can clear from there to end of screen before redrawing
# 
# But in my implementation I don't track absolute position...
# 
# Let me implement a simpler approach:
# ALWAYS do the clearing when redrawing (not just when content shrinks)
# Use [2K] on the first line, and for size changes, clear extra lines
# 
# Actually: the simplest fix is to use [2K] on EVERY line during render
# This ensures each line is cleared before writing new content
# Then after the last line, clear to end of screen with [J]
# 
# This is slightly different from original but functionally equivalent:
# - Lines within new display: cleared + rewritten
# - Lines BELOW new display: cleared by [J]

# Then: \r\n[J] (or just [J] from current position if needed)

# For SIZE-CHANGE redraws: original clears and repositions
# 
# The SIMPLEST fix: detect when new_frame_lines < prev_lines
# If shrinking: do the clearing approach
# If same or growing: do the simple overwrite approach
# 
# How to detect shrinking in my code? I'd need to render FIRST, get new line count,
# then decide which approach to use.
# 
# Actually: Let me look at what original's behavior means for the TEST:
# For test.json:
# Initial: 11 lines, go-back is 10A 27D
# After Enter (collapse root): 1 line, original does:

#   render 1 line from terminal home

# Actually, looking at the FTXUI inline screen code:

# 
# The [H] in original happens only when content SHRINKS?

# 
# So YES: [H] only happens when content changes (specifically when the clearing is needed)
# 
# OK: I'll implement the clearing behavior ALWAYS when a size-change action is taken
# But I need to know the new size BEFORE deciding whether to clear
# 
# For practical purposes: let me implement a "always clear and go to home" approach
# for ALL operations except the initial draw and initial navigation
# This would match original's behavior for collapse/expand operations
# 
# Actually: let me just implement what I see in the data:
# After Enter/+/-: use clearing approach
# After navigation: use normal approach  
# After resize: use normal approach
# 
# But I can't easily detect BEFORE rendering whether the size will change.
# 
# SIMPLEST FIX: just always use the clearing approach!
# It might not match exactly for navigation (will add extra [2K]s) but functionally works.
# 
# Actually wait: let me re-read the orig behavior for navigation:
# [10B][27C]\r[1A]*10[6n]content
# 
# After [1A]*10, cursor is at display_start (0,0) relative
# Then render: starts writing from (0,0), each line overwrites old content
# 
# For clearing approach:
# [10B][27C]\r[2K][1A][2K][1A]...[2K][J][H]
# Clear each line, move to home, render from (0,0) of TERMINAL
# 
# Key difference: clearing approach moves to TERMINAL HOME (absolute 0,0)
# Normal approach stays at display position (relative 0,0)
# 
# If display is at terminal home anyway (e.g., prompt was at top),
# both approaches give same result.
# If display is in the middle of terminal (e.g., scrolled down),
# normal approach keeps it there, clearing approach moves it to top.
# 
# For the ORIGINAL: it uses clearing approach ONLY when size changes
# This is FTXUI's behavior to handle the case where old content
# would remain visible below the new shorter content.
# 
# For my implementation:

# - When new_lines < prev_lines: use clearing approach (also resets to terminal home)
# - When new_lines >= prev_lines: use normal overwrite approach
# 
# But to know new_lines, I need to compute it BEFORE deciding the mode
# That means: compute the new render, then decide

# - on address: 11 -> 8 lines (collapse address, removing city+street+closing })

# 2. If new_lines < prev_lines: use clearing approach
# 3. Otherwise: use normal approach

# Let me modify do_render() and full_draw() to support this

echo "Implementing size-change detection..."

# [PREV_B][PREV_C]\r[2K][1A][2K][1A]...[2K][J][H][6n]
# That's: go to bottom, then [2K][1A] for each line (prev_lines times), then [2K][J][H]
# Wait: let me count:
# [2K][1A] * prev_lines = clear prev_lines lines
# But we need to go UP prev_lines lines, so [1A] * prev_lines
# But we're AT the bottom, so going up prev_lines = back to display_start
# Then [2K] for the first (current) line, [J] to clear rest of screen, [H] for home
#
# Actually: from the original test:
# [10B][27C]\r [2K][1A]*10 [2K][J][H][6n]
# That's:
# go to bottom (10B 27C)
# \r = col 0
# [2K][1A] * 10 = clear current line and go up (10 times)
# [2K][J][H] = clear current (first) line, clear to end of screen, go home
# 
# Number of [2K][1A] pairs = prev_lines - 1 = 10 (for 11-line display)
# Then [2K][J] for the topmost line
# Then [H] to go to terminal home
# 
# Total clearing: prev_lines lines cleared, then from home

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/src/json_tui.cpp', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
    
# I need to modify full_draw() to track old line count and use clearing when shrinking
# Let me update do_render() to return line count
# And update full_draw() to use clearing when needed

# The key change: full_draw needs to:
# 1. Compute new frame BEFORE deciding mode
# 2. If new < prev: use clearing mode
# 3. Otherwise: use normal mode

# Let me add a "prev_lines_saved" variable to App
old_app_decl = '    App(JPtr json, bool fs): root(build(json,"",0,true)), fullscreen(fs) {'
new_app_decl = '    int prev_lines_saved=0;  // for size-change detection\n    App(JPtr json, bool fs): root(build(json,"",0,true)), fullscreen(fs) {'

if old_app_decl in content:
    content = content.replace(old_app_decl, new_app_decl)
    print("Added prev_lines_saved to App")
else:
    print("App decl not found")

with open('/workspace/src/json_tui.cpp', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
PYEOF

echo "done"

# 
# The VISUAL behavior is correct. The cursor positioning differs but doesn't affect display.

# 1. Initial display matches original
# 2. Navigation visual output matches
# 3. Collapse/expand visual output matches
# 
# The only concern is the escape sequence byte-for-byte comparison.
# Let me check if the navigation escape sequences matter for the final display.

# For the PTY test: the CPR response [6n] causes differences when navigation happens
# because original responds differently to CPR
# But in both cases, the DISPLAY looks correct

# Let me focus on getting the DISPLAY correct and not worry too much about
# the exact cursor positioning sequences

# Let me now test the comparison WITH navigation
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import subprocess, time, os
import pty, select
import fcntl, termios, struct, re

def set_winsize(fd, rows, cols):
    winsize = struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

def get_data_keys(binary, jsonfile, keys=None, cpr_response=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    set_winsize(slave, 24, 80)
    proc = subprocess.Popen([binary, jsonfile],
        stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    data = b''
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.3)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    
    # If CPR response should be injected
    if cpr_response:
        os.write(master, cpr_response)
        time.sleep(0.05)
        while True:
            r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
            if not r: break
            try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
            except: break
    
    if keys:
        for k in keys:
            os.write(master, k)
            time.sleep(0.12)
            while True:
                r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
                if not r: break
                try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
                except: break
    os.write(master, b'q')
    time.sleep(0.2)
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: proc.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return data

# Test WITHOUT CPR responses (like in our PTY where no terminal responds)
tests_no_keys = [
    ('/tmp/simple2.json', None),
    ('/tmp/arr_root.json', None),
    ('/tmp/test.json', None),
    ('/tmp/deep.json', None),
    ('/tmp/two_objs.json', None),
    ('/tmp/table.json', None),
]

print("=== No keys (initial only) ===")
all_ok = True
for jsonfile, keys in tests_no_keys:
    orig = get_data_keys('./executable', jsonfile, keys)
    mine = get_data_keys('/tmp/json-tui-test', jsonfile, keys)
    diffs = sum(1 for a,b in zip(orig,mine) if a != b)
    same_len = len(orig) == len(mine)
    ok = diffs==0 and same_len
    if not ok: all_ok = False
    print(f"{'OK' if ok else 'DIFF'}: {jsonfile}")

print(f"\n{'ALL OK' if all_ok else 'SOME DIFFS'} (no-key tests)")
PYEOF

import subprocess, time, os
import pty, select
import fcntl, termios, struct, re

def set_winsize(fd, rows, cols):
    winsize = struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

def get_visible_frame(binary, jsonfile, keys):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    set_winsize(slave, 24, 80)
    proc = subprocess.Popen([binary, jsonfile],
        stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    data = b''
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.3)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    for k in (keys or []):
        os.write(master, k)
        time.sleep(0.15)
        while True:
            r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
            if not r: break
            try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
            except: break
    os.write(master, b'q')
    time.sleep(0.3)
    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: proc.kill()
    os.close(master)

        clean = clean.replace(b'\x00', b'').replace(b'\r', b'').replace(b'\n', b'')
        result.append(clean.decode('latin1').rstrip())
    while result and not result[-1]: result.pop()
    return result

# address becomes {...} (collapsed)
# Everything else stays same
# Root is still expanded
# 
# So '-' on a scalar: applies the same logic as '-' on parent?
# Parent of "active" = root
# '-' on root = "collapse expanded containers within root" (address gets collapsed)
# 
# But then for simple2.json: Down → "name" (scalar, parent = root)
# '-' on "name": apply '-' behavior for parent (root)
# Root has no expanded containers (name and value are scalars)
# So: collapse root itself!
# 
# CONFIRMED! The rule is:
# '-' on ANY node (including scalars):
#   Find the node to operate on:
#     if selected is a container: use selected
#     if selected is a scalar: use PARENT container
#   Then apply the collapse logic (collapse expanded children, or collapse self if none)
# 
# Let me update do_collapse() to handle this:

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/src/json_tui.cpp', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Need to add parent tracking to navigate to parent
# Currently Node doesn't track parent. Need to add parent pointer or pass through tree.

# Actually: the simplest approach is to change do_collapse():
# 1. Get selected node
# 2. If it's a scalar: get its PARENT
# 3. Call do_collapse_helper on that node

# But nodes don't have parent pointers... I need to find parent
# 
# Let me add parent pointer to Node

old_node = '''struct Node {
    JPtr val; std::string key; int depth; bool expanded=false; bool is_last=true; bool is_table=false;
    std::vector<Node> children;
    Node(JPtr v,std::string k,int d,bool last): val(v),key(std::move(k)),depth(d),is_last(last) {}
};'''

new_node = '''struct Node {
    JPtr val; std::string key; int depth; bool expanded=false; bool is_last=true; bool is_table=false;
    std::vector<Node> children;
    Node* parent=nullptr;  // parent pointer (set after build)
    Node(JPtr v,std::string k,int d,bool last): val(v),key(std::move(k)),depth(d),is_last(last) {}
};

// Set parent pointers recursively
void set_parents(Node& node) {
    for(auto& c:node.children) { c.parent=&node; set_parents(c); }
}'''

if old_node in content:
    content = content.replace(old_node, new_node)
    print("Added parent to Node!")
else:
    print("Node not found")

with open('/workspace/src/json_tui.cpp', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

import subprocess, time, os, re

import fcntl, termios, struct

    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

def get_frame(binary, jsonfile, keys):

    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    for k in (keys or []):

        time.sleep(0.12)
        while True:
            r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
            if not r: break
            try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
            except: break
    os.write(master, b'q')

    while True:
        r, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.15)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk = os.read(master, 4096); data += chunk
        except: break
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: proc.kill()
    os.close(master)
    idx = data.rfind(b'\x1b[?25l')
    if idx == -1: return []
    seg = data[max(0,idx-2000):idx]

        clean = clean.replace(b'\x00', b'').replace(b'\r', b'').replace(b'\n', b'')
        result.append(clean.decode('latin1').rstrip())

    return result

print('ALL OK!' if all_ok else 'SOME DIFFS')
